questions: Does the order of A, B, C matter? That is, are (A, B, C) and (B, A, C) considered the same triplet or distinct?
Must A, B, C be distinct integers, or can A = C even though A ≠ B and B ≠ C?
Is a 'fine triplet' defined solely by the condition that A, B, C are all in S, or is there an additional mathematical relation (like A + B = C) that makes it 'fine'?
Are we counting triplets of indices or triplets of values? Since elements are distinct, this is equivalent unless there is an ordering condition.
Should the output be the count modulo some number, or the exact integer count?
Is the set S given as sorted or in arbitrary order?
Can the triplet (A, B, C) be formed by reusing the same element if indices are considered? (But elements are distinct, so A=B is already excluded.)
Is there any constraint on the relative sizes of A, B, C (like A < B < C) that would affect counting?
